title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-acme
content:
Account: Acme Logistics (Acme) -- quick scratchpad

Notes to self / context:
- Got introduced via Ryan (met at FreightTech conf). Prospect seemed receptive to latency/cost issues.
- Acme is exploring LLMs for automated support triage + multimodal routing (docs + invoices). We position Redwood as low-latency, cost-predictable inference layer they can run in cloud or VPC.
- Hypothesis: procurement will push back on custom infra costs; engineering cares about throughput and SLOs.

High-level account research (public + notes):
- HQ: Chicago. ~3k employees. Logistics + TMS product.
- Recent funding: Series D 2024 (press release).
- Tech org: central platform team + domain engineering for operations. Uses GCP and some on-prem for sensitive workloads.
- Likely priorities: reduce ticket deflection time, automate invoice parsing, improve SLA for carrier communications (low latency token-level inference).

Key contacts (try to confirm via LinkedIn):
- Priya Shah -- Dir of Platform Engineering (decision maker for infra choices) -- target for technical deep dive.
- Marcus Lee -- Head of ML/AI (influencer) -- cares about model evaluations, embeddings quality.
- Jenna Torres -- VP Customer Ops (user champion) -- cares about cost per ticket, accuracy.

Why Redwood matters (value props to hit):
- Predictable unit economics: batching + KV cache reduces token cost without sacrificing latency. Good for high query volumes (support triage).
- Flexible deployment: can start with hosted API for quick POC, then move to Dedicated or Private for compliance and cost control.
- Observability: per-route cost/latency breakdowns and rollouts to catch regressions during model upgrades.

Pain points to validate on discovery call:
- Are you seeing inconsistent latency or high tail latencies when routing to LLM endpoints?
- How are you currently pricing/forecasting token spend for support automation?
- Any constraints on data residency / need for private deployment?
- Current QA/regression process for model changes? How often do you see quality drops?

Quick technical notes (for convo prep):
- Redwood supports prefix+KV caching to speed repeated conversation context. Useful for support threads.
- For invoice parsing, recommend embeddings + reranking to narrow candidate spans before extraction. Could propose small eval run with their sample prompts.

Outbound email drafts (A/B test these):
- Subject A: Quick idea to cut support triage time by 30%
- Subject B: Acme + Redwood -- cheaper, faster LLM inference for support

Draft 1 (short):
Hi Priya --
Saw Acme's note about scaling customer automation. I work on partnerships at Redwood Inference -- we help teams run LLM inference with predictable latency and unit costs (hosted -> private). Would love 20m to share a quick POC plan for reducing support triage time using KV caching + dedicated inference. Any chance next week?
-- Olivia

Draft 2 (technical):
Hi Marcus / Priya --
Quick note: we run a 2-week POC for customers in logistics where we show 3 things: 1) median+95th latency under target, 2) cost per resolved ticket, 3) regression monitoring on your test prompts. For invoice parsing we can run a small batch eval on your sample invoices and show accuracy + cost delta vs your current pipeline. If useful, I can share a one-pager and a proposed timeline.

LinkedIn connection note (very short):
Hi Priya -- enjoyed your talk at FreightTech. Would love to connect and share a quick idea on improving support automation latency.

Call script / discovery checklist (bullet style):
- 1-2 min intro + context (why Redwood, quick wins)
- Ask current infra: cloud provider(s), on-prem needs, traffic volume (#queries/day, avg tokens, peak QPS)
- SLA targets: median/95th latency goals; cost targets per ticket or per 1k queries
- Data controls: PII, encryption, KMS requirements
- Model ops: who owns model rollouts? need for canary/A-B policies?
- Proof points: cite similar customer (anonymized) where we reduced cost 25% with batching + cache.

Objection handling (common objections + rebuttals):
- "We can't move to a new vendor" -> "Start with hosted API POC (no infra change), evaluate performance/cost for 2-4 weeks, then decide on Dedicated/Private."
- "We already have a model infra team" -> "Great -- Redwood can act as a standardized runtime and orchestration layer without replacing your stack; or we can run side-by-side comparison and show unit-cost differences."
- "Security/compliance concerns" -> "Private deployment with customer VPC and KMS integration, audit logs; happy to share SOC2 artifacts and architecture diagram."
- "Worried about output quality when optimizing cost" -> "We run evals tied to your prompt set and track regressions; suggest canary rollout and automatic fallback to a higher-quality variant if regression detected."

Demo ideas / POC outline (2-week lightweight):
- Week 0: onboarding + data collection (sample tickets/invoices, prompts)
- Week 1: run evals on sample set + configure caching and batching; show latency/cost baseline vs Redwood baseline
- Week 2: run live POC on subset of traffic (shadow or small %), provide dashboard with cost/latency/accuracy metrics
- Success criteria: 10-30% reduction in cost per resolved ticket OR 20% improvement in 95th latency while preserving accuracy

Open questions / follow-ups for Ryan / internal:
- Need a 1-pager + architecture slide for Priya (include VPC/private option).
- Ask Solutions Eng for rough estimate on Dedicated capacity needed for 50k qps bursts (tag: SE-quick-est).
- Can we get anonymized case study reference for logistics customer? (Danielle chasing)

Tasks / next steps (owner initials):
- Draft 1-pager + proposed timeline (Olivia) -- due 2026-02-23
- Book intro call w/ Priya (Olivia) -- target week of 2/24
- Internal SE sync to validate cost estimates (Ryan) -- target 2/21

Notes: keep this doc messy -- will iterate after call.
